newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Lyonnais silent on securitisation report.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais silent on securitisation report.

text.p: French state-controlled bank Crdit Lyonnais declined comment on Thursday on a report it would securitise around 10 billion francs in real estate loans as part of an effort to improve its balance sheet.
Business daily L'Agefi said the offering would bring to more than 68 billion francs the amount of loans securitised by the bank since 1991.
Credit Lyonnais nearly collapsed in the early 1990s, after a lending spree that briefly turned it into the largest bank outside Japan, but now is on the road to recovery.
The newspaper said the debt mutual fund (fonds commun de creances) would be dubbed Titrilog and was being studied for approval by the French regulatory authorities.
It said the operation would syndicated like a classic bond operation and be done in three tranches.

There would be two primary issues with maturities of between two and five years carrying triple AAA ratings and one subordinated issue with a maturity of about five and half years bearing a single A rating.
Securitisation is widely used in the United States to repackage debt into negotiable shares and has become increasingly popular in France.
Credit Lyonnais has carried out several such operations in a bid to ease pressure on its balance sheet and seek refinancing at a more modest cost.
In 1996,the bank carried out a 40 billion franc securitisation issue. The deal was the largest ever sale of non-government bonds anywhere in the world.
